requirements.description: the visible acceptance check passes on a fresh checkout

When a Header is constructed with an explicit negative size in its data object, that negative size should be ignored and remain undefined. (the task: "header data whose size is negative when compared as a number, whether passed to the constructor (new Header({ size: -1000 })) or merged in from an extended header, is ignored, so header.size stays undefined")

Header constructor with positive sizes should continue to work correctly. (the task: "every other field (uid, gid, mode, the times and so on) keeps its current parsing, negative values included, and nothing else changes")

uncheckedRequirements.description: When a Header decodes a block with negative size (base-256 encoded starting with 0xff), or when extended headers provide negative sizes, the final size should be undefined. (the task: "when a block is decoded, the size it computes (the extended header's size, else the global extended header's size, else the block's own size field) becomes undefined if it is negative")

Pax.parse with valid (zero or positive) size records should continue to work as before. (the task: "every other field (uid, gid, mode, the times and so on) keeps its current parsing, negative values included, and nothing else changes")

Pax.parse should keep size undefined when the 'size' record has a negative numeric value. (the task: "In Pax.parse, a 'size' record is kept only when its numeric value is zero or greater: 'size=-1000' and a non-numeric value leave size undefined, while 'size=1000' gives 1000 and 'size=0' gives 0.")

Pax.parse should keep size undefined when the 'size' record has a non-numeric value. (the task: "In Pax.parse, a 'size' record is kept only when its numeric value is zero or greater: 'size=-1000' and a non-numeric value leave size undefined")
